# Write: Your own study

## Create your study report

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/create_report.R your-study
```

Open `reports/your-study-report.qmd`. Use your own values throughout; synthetic and Zeisel numbers are worked examples, not values to transfer into your report. The helper preserves existing writing.

## Turn notes into a defensible account

| Section | Evidence to include |
|---|---|
| Question and data | Source, organism, assay, raw-count units, samples/donors and known design limits |
| Methods | Input checks, annotation, justified QC rules, transformation and PCA choices |
| Results | Actual cell counts, sample-specific retention where known, figures and variance percentages |
| Verification | An exact cell ID, manual/saved values and verifier outcome |
| Interpretation | Observations, possible explanations and evidence still needed |
| AI use | The assistance received and your checks of it |
| Next step | A justified follow-up matched to the unresolved question |

An observation such as “one sample lost a larger fraction of cells” can be reported if the saved table supports it. An explanation such as “that sample was damaged” requires additional evidence. Similarly, separated PCA regions do not by themselves establish a condition effect.

Keep the denominator visible: “X of Y input cells passed the configured rules.” If QC choices were revised, describe the final rationale and note the decision process. Do not select only the most attractive plot from several undocumented runs.

## Render and inspect

```bash
cd reports
quarto render your-study-report.qmd
cd ..
```

Read `reports/your-study-report.html`. Both figures should display using paths under `../results/your-study/figures/`. Confirm every number against its source, remove bracketed starter instructions and record software/input provenance. Embedded images make HTML convenient to share but do not remove private information from it; inspect content before distribution.

## Final learner review

Can another reader find your raw input source, understand the retention rule, repeat one cell calculation and distinguish your observations from interpretation? If not, revise the relevant section before sharing.

**Your task:** identify the strongest supported conclusion and the most important limitation. State one next action that would address that limitation rather than simply repeat the same plot.

Keep the report and generated HTML inside ignored `reports/`. Publish or share a reviewed report deliberately; do not add private learner outputs to the book's chapter list.
